story:
Amy skipped into Sunny Meadow Park, her blue bucket swinging. Today was special because her friend, Leo, was coming to build the biggest, most magnificent sandcastle ever! She saw many children already digging near the sparkling pond, creating little sand *mounds* and *rivers*. Amy felt a flutter of excitement in her tummy, mixed with a little bit of nervousness about starting such a grand project. She really hoped Leo would arrive soon.

“Amy! Over here!” Leo waved from a patch of damp sand. He was carrying his own red shovel and a big smile. “Let’s make a castle with so many *towers* and a super-long *wall*!” Amy grinned. They got to work, but soon realized a problem. All the best *buckets* and *spades* were being used by a group of older kids building a giant volcano. Amy felt a little worried. How could they build a magnificent castle without enough tools? She tried to scoop handfuls of sand, but it kept crumbling. “This is hard,” she sighed, a bit frustrated.

Leo, always thinking, pointed to a small, shy girl named Maya who was carefully decorating tiny sand *cakes* nearby. She had several colorful *pails* and some extra *shovels* tucked beside her. “Maybe we could borrow some?” Leo suggested. Amy took a deep breath. She walked over to Maya, feeling a little brave. “Excuse me, Maya,” Amy began, "Would you mind if we borrowed one of your *pails*? We want to build a really big castle with many *bridges*.” Maya looked up, her eyes wide. “My *friends* like to use all the *toys*,” she mumbled, looking down at her cakes. Leo chimed in, “We could even build a connecting *road* from our castle to your sand village, so our *knights* could visit your *princesses*!” Maya’s eyes lit up. “A road?” she whispered, a small smile forming. “Okay, you can use these two *shovels* and this yellow *pail*.” Amy felt a wave of relief, so grateful for Maya’s kindness.

Working together, Amy, Leo, and Maya shared tools, laughing as they poured water and packed the wet, cool sand. Amy described the *flags* she imagined on top of their highest tower. Leo used Maya’s extra spade to carve a winding path. Soon, their castle was tall and strong, with tiny *windows* and *doors*, and a perfect road leading right to Maya’s little sand village. Amy felt so proud of what they had built, not just the castle, but the new friendship with Maya. "This is the best castle ever!" she exclaimed, feeling excited and happy.
